findings.summary: The term "selectivity" is used on page 1 and again on page 2 as a tie-break rule, but the chapter never defines it.
findings.evidence: "Low-selectivity columns (gender, boolean) rarely help" and "Break ties by higher selectivity"
findings.fix: On page 1, add a one-line definition: selectivity is the fraction of rows a value filters out. A column with many distinct values is highly selective, and a boolean is not.

findings.summary: The leftmost-prefix table says a filter on b or c alone can never use an (a, b, c) index, which is no longer true on several engines.
findings.evidence:
b alone | no
c alone | no
findings.fix: Qualify the rule, e.g. 'b alone | usually no (Oracle, MySQL 8.0 and PostgreSQL 18+ can use skip scan when a has few distinct values, but it is slow)'. Make the same change in the page 6 leftmost-prefix line and the page 7 'city is skipped' answer.

findings.summary: Two CREATE INDEX statements with the same name sit in one code block, so a learner can't tell they are alternatives.
findings.fix: Split into two labelled snippets (Postgres/SQL Server and MySQL), or use different index names and put the engine in a comment above each statement.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "conversion", "implicit").
findings.evidence: Implicit type conversion: comparing a VARCHAR column to a number (WHERE phone = 5551234) forces a cast on every row and skips the index
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "selectivity", "optimizer").
findings.evidence: Low selectivity or tiny table: the optimizer picks a full scan when the query returns a large share of rows (often more than roughly 10-20%) because random lookups would cost more
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The code block joins two unrelated fixes (range rewrite and functional index) under one caption.
findings.evidence:
WHERE created_at >= '2025-01-01'
  AND created_at <  '2026-01-01'
CREATE INDEX idx_email_lower
  ON users (LOWER(email));
rewrite the predicate, or index the expression
findings.fix: Show two separate snippets, each with a one-line caption: 'range on bare column' and 'functional index on LOWER(email)'.

findings.summary: The 'More skips' bullets list cases without saying why the index is skipped.
findings.evidence:
OR across different columns
<> and NOT IN
findings.fix: Add a short reason to each, such as 'OR across columns: one index can't serve both branches' and '<> and NOT IN: match almost all rows, so there is no narrow range to seek'.

findings.summary: The type-mismatch row says the column is cast and the index skipped, but page 7 says PostgreSQL errors instead.
findings.evidence: Type mismatch: VARCHAR vs number casts every row ... phone = 5551234 | phone = '5551234'
findings.fix: Note the engine split here: MySQL and SQL Server cast every row and skip the index; Postgres raises an error.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "definition", "execution").
findings.evidence: Definition: EXPLAIN shows the planned execution without running the query; EXPLAIN ANALYZE (Postgres, MySQL 8) runs it and adds actual times and row counts
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: 'Sargable' is the page title but is only defined in section 3, after the plan-reading sections.
findings.evidence: Sargable = can seek an index: keep the bare column on one side
findings.fix: Add a one-line definition of 'sargable' at the top of the page or move section 3 first.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "referential", "integrity").
findings.evidence: FOREIGN KEY enforces referential integrity with ON DELETE CASCADE / SET NULL / RESTRICT; the engine does not auto-index the child column in Postgres or SQL Server, so index FK columns yourself to speed joins and parent deletes
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: Single bullets combine two ideas, and the DML syntax lines have no stated idea or code label.
findings.evidence:
Run UPDATE and DELETE in a transaction with a WHERE
INSERT and DELETE touch all indexes; UPDATE touches those with a changed column
findings.fix: Split each into one-idea bullets, and put the INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE syntax in a labelled sql snippet after a one-line idea such as 'every write also updates the indexes'.

findings.summary: The design rule orders equality, then ORDER BY, then range columns, but page 2 states only 'equality first, range last' and never mentions ORDER BY columns.
findings.evidence: Equality cols → ORDER BY cols → Range col  vs  'Equality columns first, range column last'
findings.fix: Add the ORDER BY placement to page 2's Column Order section so the cheat sheet repeats what the chapter taught.
